extracted.intended_audience: New York state agency staff, regulated parties, attorneys, and members of the public who prepare or respond to rulemaking notices and participate in NY notice-and-comment rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards from the New York State Administrative Procedure Act governing how agencies must prepare, publish, and support public notice-and-comment rulemaking (including required contents of notices, timing, required analyses, accessibility, and related procedural obligations). Useful for drafting notices, regulatory impact/job‑impact statements, small business guides, and complying with disclosure and posting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and clarity of rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall strive to ensure that, to the maximum extent practical, its rules, regulations and related documents are written in a clear and coherent manner, using words with common and everyday meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory minimum: agencies may adopt additional procedures so long as they are not inconsistent with statute. The requirement applies to rule text and related documents (e.g., notices, guides) and supports accessibility and comprehension by regulated parties and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'rule' (scope of APA)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rule" means (i) the whole or part of each agency statement, regulation or code of general applicability that implements or applies law, or prescribes a fee charged by or paid to any agency or the procedure or practice requirements of any agency..." (with enumerated exclusions such as internal management, forms/instructions, interpretive statements, certain low-dollar fees, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines whether APA rulemaking procedures (notice, comment, analyses) apply. Agencies must assess whether a proposed action fits the statutory definition of rule and check listed exclusions to determine procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'substantial revision'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Substantial revision" means any addition, deletion or other change in the text of a rule proposed for adoption, which materially alters its purpose, meaning or effect, but shall not include any change which merely defines or clarifies such text and does not materially alter its purpose, meaning or effect...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decide whether a revised proposed rule requires new notice of proposed rulemaking. Comparison is made against the text for which prior notice was published (or most recent revised notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus rule (expedited) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: "Consensus rule" means a rule proposed by an agency for adoption on an expedited basis pursuant to the expectation that no person is likely to object to its adoption because it merely (a) repeals regulatory provisions which are no longer applicable to any person, (b) implements or conforms to non-discretionary statutory provisions, or (c) makes technical changes or is otherwise non-controversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may use streamlined procedures for consensus rules but must include a clear and concise explanation of the basis for the determination that no person is likely to object. If any public comment objects, the agency must withdraw the consensus notice and proceed under full rulemaking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of notice of proposed rule making (publication and comment period)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the adoption of a rule, an agency shall submit a notice of proposed rule making to the secretary of state for publication in the state register and shall afford the public an opportunity to submit comments... the notice of proposed rule making must appear in the state register at least sixty days prior to either (i) the addition, amendment or repeal of a rule for which statute does not require that a public hearing be held prior to adoption, or (ii) the first public hearing on a proposed rule for which such hearing is so required. The notice shall indicate the last date for submission of comments, which, unless a different time is specified in statute, shall be not less than sixty days after the date of publication... or, if statute requires a public hearing, not less than five days after the date of the last public hearing scheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure minimum publication lead times and set comment deadlines accordingly. Statutory exceptions can alter timing. For consensus rules some notice requirements may be waived per statute (see consensus rule criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirements (mandatory elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of proposed rule making shall: (i) cite the statutory authority under which the rule is proposed; (ii) give date, time and place of any public hearings; (iii) state whether hearings will be reasonably accessible to persons with mobility impairments; (iv) include a statement that interpreter services will be made available to deaf persons upon written request and related interpreter rules; (v) contain the complete text of the proposed rule (or, if the text exceeds 2,000 words, a description of subject/purpose/substance in <2,000 words and the address of the website where the full text is posted); (vi) include a regulatory impact statement (or a summary if >2,000 words) and (vii) include regulatory flexibility and rural area flexibility analyses (or summaries if >2,000 words); (viii) give the name, public office address and telephone number of an agency representative knowledgeable on the proposed rule from whom materials may be obtained and to whom comments may be submitted; and (ix) include any additional matter required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory checklist for what must appear in the notice. Agencies must prepare required analyses and ensure posting and summaries per length limits. Inclusion of contact info obligates agencies to provide supporting materials on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of full text and online availability when notice is descriptive
rubrics_metrics.description: When the notice contains only a description of the subject, purpose and substance of the rule because the full text exceeds two thousand words, the full text of the proposed rule shall be posted on a website maintained by the agency or another state entity and shall remain posted until such proposed rule is adopted, revised, withdrawn or expires... the notice shall identify the address of the website on which the full text has been posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rule text too long for full inclusion in the state register notice, agencies must ensure continuous online availability and include the URL in the notice. This ensures public access to the full proposed text throughout the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory impact, regulatory flexibility, and rural area analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include a regulatory impact statement prepared pursuant to section 202‑a, and include a regulatory flexibility analysis and a rural area flexibility analysis prepared pursuant to sections 202‑b and 202‑bb; if any such statement or analysis exceeds two thousand words, the notice shall include only a summary in less than two thousand words and the full text shall be posted on a website until revised or the proposed rule is adopted/withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must complete these analyses when required and make them available to the public (with summaries in the notice if lengthy). Separate statutory provisions (202‑a, 202‑b, 202‑bb) define contents and triggers for these analyses; failure to include or post properly can affect procedural compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job impact objective and duty to minimize adverse job effects
rubrics_metrics.description: In developing a rule, an agency shall strive to accomplish the objectives of applicable statutes in a manner which minimizes any unnecessary adverse impacts on existing jobs and promotes the development of new employment opportunities, including opportunities for self‑employment, for the residents of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching objective informs preparation of job impact statements and the agency's substantive consideration of employment consequences when drafting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job impact evaluation triggers and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Before proposing or adopting a rule on an emergency basis, an agency shall evaluate the potential impact of the rule on jobs and employment opportunities. If it is apparent the rule will not have a substantial adverse impact, include in the notice a statement of that determination and, where appropriate, indicate positive or no impact and summarize the information and methodology underlying the determination. If the rule may have a substantial adverse impact, the agency shall issue a job impact statement containing: (i) the nature of the impact; (ii) categories of jobs affected; (iii) approximate number of jobs affected in each category; (iv) regions of the state with disproportionate adverse impact; and (v) measures the agency has taken to minimize adverse impacts and promote new opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The job impact statement must be substantive and include methodology and measures. "Substantial adverse impact" is defined in statute (e.g., decrease of more than 100 full‑time annual jobs over two years) and triggers the detailed statement requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job impact procedural rules (insufficient information, revisions, emergency rules, summaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: If available information is insufficient to determine whether a rule will have a substantial adverse impact, the agency shall issue a statement identifying the information needed and request assistance. The agency shall issue a revised job impact statement when the original is inadequate or when substantial revisions to the proposed rule occur. When adopting a rule on an emergency basis, an agency may defer the issuance of the job impact statement but must publish it in the state register within thirty days of the effective date. When any job impact statement exceeds two thousand words, the agency shall prepare a summary under two thousand words for publication in the state register and identify the website where the full text is posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural safeguards ensure transparency even when complete information is not initially available or when emergency adoptions occur. Summaries must be prepared for long statements to keep notices readable while full analyses are posted online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioners' review and statement of concurrence (job impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner of labor and the commissioner of economic development may review any job impact statement and may consult informally with any agency preparing such a statement and advise it. If they concur that additional evaluation is needed, they shall issue a statement of concurrence identifying the proposed rule, basis for additional evaluation, recommendations, and a time period (not more than 90 days) for action; the statement of concurrence shall be considered public comment and summarized and analyzed in assessment of public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency must consider and respond to such concurrence before adopting the rule or wait until the time period lapses; any concurrence is treated as public comment and must be incorporated into the public comment assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and interpreter services for hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice must state whether the place of any public hearing shall be reasonably accessible to persons with a mobility impairment. The notice must include a statement that interpreter services shall be made available to deaf persons, at no charge, upon written request to a designated agency representative within a reasonable time prior to any scheduled hearing. If requested, the agency shall appoint a qualified interpreter certified by a recognized authority. The agency shall determine a reasonable fee for interpreting services which shall be a charge upon the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must plan for physical accessibility and language access at hearings and must identify a representative to receive accommodation requests. A failure of accessibility despite diligent effort does not invalidate actions taken at hearings, but agencies should document efforts to provide accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency representative and disclosure obligations in notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice shall give the name, public office address and telephone number of an agency representative, who is knowledgeable on the proposed rule, from whom the complete text of the rule and any scientific or statistical study, report and analysis that served as the basis for the rule and any supporting data, the regulatory impact statement, the regulatory flexibility analysis, and the rural area flexibility analysis may be obtained; from whom information about any public hearing may be obtained; and to whom written data, views and arguments may be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligates agencies to provide materials on request and identifies the point of contact for public participation. Agencies must ensure the representative can actually supply or arrange access to the listed materials within statutory timeframes (e.g., 30 days for studies/data under Section 104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to studies, reports, analyses and supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency, upon request, shall, within thirty days, make available for inspection and copying any scientific or statistical study, report or analysis... that is used as the basis of a proposed rule and any supporting data; provided, however, the agency shall provide for inspection only of any such study, report or analysis due to copyright restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must respond promptly to requests for foundational materials. Contracts or grants for such studies must require the contractor/grantee to provide the study, supporting data, and identify the principal persons who performed the study for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract/grant terms to secure studies and data
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency that contracts with a person or entity for the performance of a study or awards a grant for such purpose shall require as a condition or term of such contract or grant that the person or entity shall provide to the agency the study, any data supporting the study, and identity of the principal person or persons who performed such study for disclosure in accordance with Section 104 and article six of the public officers law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must include disclosure and delivery requirements in contracts/grants to ensure studies used in rulemaking can be released to the public under the 30‑day rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice expiration, continuation, and withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of proposed rule making shall expire and be ineffective for the purposes of the section unless the proposed rule is adopted and filed within 365 days after the later of publication or the date of the last public hearing; if a notice expires, the secretary of state shall publish a notice of expiration. If, within 90 days of expiration, an agency submits a notice of revised rule making, rulemaking will be continued for an additional 90 days. An agency may withdraw a notice of proposed rule making by submitting a notice of withdrawal which shall include a statement of the reason(s) for withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must track statutory expiration periods; withdrawing requires stating reasons in the public record. Revised notices filed within specified windows can extend or continue the rulemaking without restarting from scratch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of revised rule making and description of objections
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency submits a notice of proposed rule making for a rule which was proposed as a consensus rule and subsequently withdrawn, such notice shall identify the prior notice of proposed rule making and shall briefly describe the objection(s) which caused the prior notice to be withdrawn. Notice of revised rule making has procedural prerequisites set in statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about prior objections helps the public understand changes and agency responses. Agencies must clearly identify prior notices and the nature of objections when re‑noticing rules after withdrawn consensus attempts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries when statements/analyses exceed word limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When any required statement or analysis (e.g., proposed rule text, regulatory impact statement, regulatory flexibility analysis, job impact statement) exceeds two thousand words, the agency shall include a summary of such statement in less than two thousand words in the state register notice and identify the website where the full text of the statement has been posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances readability of the state register notice with public access to full technical analyses online. Agencies should prepare concise summaries that accurately reflect methodological bases and key conclusions of longer documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to treat series of related rules as one rule for job impact
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may consider a series of closely related and simultaneously proposed rules as one rule for the purpose of submitting a consolidated job impact statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple related rules have aggregate employment effects, agencies may prepare a single consolidated analysis rather than separate statements for each rule; must ensure consolidated analysis addresses the statutory content elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoptions and procedural deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the job impact section shall be construed as preventing an agency from adopting a rule on an emergency basis at any time. When adopting a rule on an emergency basis, an agency may defer issuance of job impact statements but must publish the required statement in the state register within thirty days of the effective date of the emergency rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency adoptions can deviate from ordinary timing but agencies remain required to complete and publish analyses within statutory post‑adoption deadlines.
